name: maya-s1
description: Maya Chen, Session 1 (Before the Title). Articulate executive persona — tests the clean voice path, the Part 1A position ladder, the principle-naming gate, and the refinement question. Synthetic but representative of the Maya persona; replace with a PII-scrubbed real session when one is available.
userTurns: I'm tired of trying to explain what I actually do. My LinkedIn reads like a healthcare operations resume but that's not the through-line. Every role keeps reshaping itself around what someone else needs, and I keep adapting, and at some point I lost the thread of what's mine in any of it.

When I left my last consulting role. I'd been passed over for partner twice. I kept being the person they brought in to save troubled engagements but my utilization metrics were complicated because I spent too much time on knowledge sharing and mentoring. I realized I was good at the thing nobody was measuring.
Yeah. That lands. I see it now — the thing I'm best at is the thing that doesn't fit in the boxes the org wants to measure.

When I was a kid, my parents ran a dry cleaner in Queens. My dad spoke limited English so my mom handled the front. By the time I was seven I was the unofficial translator — not just of language but of meaning. A customer would be upset about a stain and I'd figure out what was really going on underneath: a job interview, a wedding, a funeral. I'd help my mom respond to that, not just the complaint.

I made systems for my brother. Color-coded homework folders. Chore charts broken into steps he could actually do. When he struggled with math I'd figure out how he learned and rebuild the explanation around that. It didn't occur to me that this was unusual — I just couldn't function in chaos.
